newsitem.title: CANADA: CRICKET-OFFICIALS HOPE CANADA SERIES WILL START SUNDAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-OFFICIALS HOPE CANADA SERIES WILL START SUNDAY.

text.p: Sporadic showers hampered an eight-hour mop up to prepare Canada's lone first class turf cricket wicket for Sunday's opening match of the Sahara Cup international series here.
Saturday's scheduled match between India and Pakistan was postponed on Friday when torrential rain flooded the lush Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling Club ground.
Officials worked throughout Saturday to soak up the pools of water around the ground and took the covers off the wicket area for a time in the morning to allow moisture to escape.
However occasional afternoon showers added to the woes of Canadian cricket officials who were poised to host the first full series of one-day matches between India and Pakistan since 1989.
Sahara Cup spokesman Tony McWatt said Sunday's opening match was still on.

However, further heavy rain overnight was likely to put the fixture in doubt. If the umpires were forced to abandon the day's play after an inspection of the ground on Sunday morning, the match would be re-scheduled for Tuesday.
Officials already announced Saturday's wash out would be held on Monday.
The third match of the series was scheduled for Wednesday (the 18th) with the fourth and fifth encounters next weekend.

With a lack of suitable cricket training facilities in Toronto where the game is popular only amongst the immigrant communities from the Caribbean and the Sub Continent, players from both sides spent the day touring the region.
Wasim Akram's Pakistan side, fresh from a Test series victory over England, headed to nearby Niagara Falls.
